title: Arize AZ 7888 (NSIC Rc 494H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Arize AZ 7888 (NSIC Rc 494H) Rice: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Arize AZ 7888 is NSIC Rc 494H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 113 days and 6 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 494H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as Arize AZ 7888 or AZ 7888 and known locally as Mestiso 84. The NSIC approved it in 2017. Bayer bred it. It matures in about 113 days and averages 6 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 12.6 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Arize AZ 7888 or AZ 7888, or rice variety 494H, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 6 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 120 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 12.6 tonnes.
**Cooked rice:** intermediate amylose, so soft but not sticky.

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 494H yield?

On average it gives 6 tonnes per hectare. That is about 120 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids on the list, which is 6.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 12.6 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 113 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

items: **Days to harvest:** 106 to 110 days after sowing.
**How it is planted:** Direct seeded or transplanted.
**Seed:** 21 to 24 kg per hectare direct seeded, 15 kg transplanted.
About 115 cm tall, with 14 to 24 productive tillers.
Long slender grain, with a milling recovery of 60 to 65 percent in the national trials and head rice of 50.3 percent.
Cooks slightly aromatic, white, glossy, soft and sticky.
Bred to tolerate bacterial leaf blight.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual variety on the same ground.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant together with the farms around you, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is Arize AZ 7888 the same as NSIC Rc 494H?
items.a: Yes. Arize AZ 7888 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 494H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 84. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 494H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 494H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 84. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 494H take to harvest?
items.a: About 113 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 494H?
items.a: It averages 6 tonnes per hectare, about 120 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 12.6 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: It is recommended for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.
